tasks.short: Check and approve payment requests and the weekly Rabobank payment batch against budget, contract and policy.

today.trigger: Invoices reach approval status in AFAS, agency invoices arrive from the three portals, and the weekly payment batch is ready for release.
steps: Open the AFAS approval queue and the draft payment batch
Compare large or unusual invoices with the purchase order, contract or agency hours
Check for duplicates and changed IBANs by hand, often in Excel
Ask budget holders by Outlook or Teams about items that do not match
Approve in AFAS and co-sign the batch in Rabobank
drudgery: Matching agency invoices to approved hours line by line
Scanning for duplicate invoice numbers and IBAN changes
Chasing budget holders for approvals
today.time_sinks: Flex worker invoices from three agencies in peak season, and waiting for budget holders to reply.

lenses.faster: Rule checks for budget, contract, duplicate, IBAN change and agency hours against invoice run on every item, so the controller only opens the flagged ones and items above the threshold; time drops from about 3 hours a week to about 1.
lenses.autonomous: An invoice entering the AFAS approval flow triggers the checks; clean items under the threshold go to the batch, and the controller approves flagged and large items before the Rabobank batch is released.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: a weekly check of agency invoices against the hours they signed off, so overbilling on flex workers is caught every week instead of at year end; demand grows as the checks get cheaper because peak season adds volume.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses ticking invoice numbers against a spreadsheet; the controller wants more time on the few odd payments and on fixing the policy that lets them through.
lenses.options: Little value in several drafts; the decision is approve or hold, though testing two approval thresholds on last year's batches shows the trade-off between risk and workload.
lenses.altitude: The controller's week shifts from approving items to setting thresholds, owning the check rules and reviewing the exception log monthly; the job becomes more expert in control design.
reach: Bookkeeper (accounts payable): first-line invoice matching, needing knowledge of the check rules
Finance Director: second signature on the batch, needing a clear mandate register

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an unusual payment makes business sense, spotting social-engineering fraud such as a supplier IBAN change by phone, and holding signing authority.
tasks.pattern_why: Budget, contract, duplicate and IBAN-change checks are written rules on AFAS and portal data; no model is needed to run them.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice reaches approval status in AFAS or the payment batch is drafted.
steps: Pull invoice, PO, budget and supplier master data from AFAS
Match agency invoices to approved hours from the portals
Run duplicate, IBAN-change, budget and threshold rules
Pass clean small items to the batch and queue the rest with the reason
Controller approves the queue and releases the batch in Rabobank
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every flagged item and every item above the amount threshold before the Rabobank batch is released.
data_needed: Supplier master with IBAN change history
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history plus an exception log on SharePoint kept for the auditor.

evidence.claim: The digest recommends deterministic checks for budget, contract, duplicate and IBAN change at autonomy 3, with a person approving above a threshold.
AFAS matching works on fixed rules on reference, IBAN and invoice number.
Cash allocation needs mandatory human review and timestamped logs.

risks: Rules too loose let fraud through; too tight and the queue does not shrink
Agency portal exports may differ in format and break matching
Auto-passing small items invites invoice splitting
research_questions: What share of last year's invoices would have passed all rules cleanly?
Can the three agency portals export hours in a stable format or by API?
How many IBAN changes per year occurred, and were any fraudulent?

tasks.short: Watch daily cash position, credit facility headroom and filing and tax deadlines so nothing is breached.

today.trigger: Each morning, plus month-end and VAT and payroll tax deadlines.
steps: Download Rabobank statements and check the balance against the cash plan in Excel
Look at large expected receipts and payments for the coming weeks
Check covenant and facility headroom monthly
Track VAT, payroll tax and KVK filing dates in a calendar
Warn the Finance Director when something drifts
drudgery: Copying bank balances into the cash sheet
Rebuilding the weekly cash forecast by hand
Keeping a deadline list up to date
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the rolling cash forecast from AFAS AR and AP ageing every week.

lenses.faster: A daily job reads the CAMT.053 statement and AFAS open items, updates the 13-week cash view and checks covenant and deadline rules, so the controller reads one alert page in 10 minutes instead of building it.
lenses.autonomous: The overnight bank file and the AFAS extract trigger the run; the controller only acts on alerts that cross a set threshold.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: the cash forecast and covenant check become daily instead of weekly or monthly, which matters in peak season when agency invoices spike; demand would grow because the Finance Director would use it in every supplier and customer talk.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying balances into Excel; the controller wants more time explaining why cash moved.
lenses.options: Low; a single forecast with clear drivers is enough here, scenarios belong to the funding task.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the alert thresholds and the deadline calendar and gets a weekly cash talk with the Finance Director instead of a spreadsheet; slightly more expert.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: daily view of overdue receivables feeding cash
FP&A Analyst: the short-term cash forecast, needing driver-based modelling

tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a big customer will pay late before it shows in the data, and deciding when to tell the bank.
tasks.pattern_why: Balances, ageing, covenant ratios and deadlines are calculations and rules on structured bank and AFAS data.

in_practice.trigger: Arrival of the overnight Rabobank CAMT.053 file and nightly AFAS extract.
steps: Load bank balances and AFAS open AR and AP
Update the 13-week cash view in Power BI
Check facility headroom, covenant ratios and minimum cash
Check the compliance calendar for upcoming VAT, loonheffing and KVK deadlines
Send an alert to the controller only when a rule fires
in_practice.human_gate: The controller decides on any action on an alert, such as drawing the facility or delaying a payment.
data_needed: AFAS open items and payment terms
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI history and an alert log in a SharePoint list.

evidence.claim: Cash and deposit handling is near zero work with SEPA batches and CAMT.053.
Cash allocation should stay under mandatory human review with timestamped logs.

risks: Forecast trusted too much when payment behaviour of big customers changes
False alerts make people ignore the feed
research_questions: How far off was last year's weekly cash forecast, and from which drivers?
Does Rabobank deliver CAMT.053 automatically to a location the job can read?
Which covenant definitions in the facility agreement can be calculated from AFAS data alone?

tasks.short: Work out when we need extra financing or can park surplus cash, and advise the Finance Director.

today.trigger: Cash forecast shows a dip or surplus, a large investment such as forklifts or a site expansion, or the yearly facility review.
steps: Take the cash forecast and capex plans from Excel
Model scenarios for a facility draw, lease or deposit
Ask Rabobank and lessors for terms
Write a short recommendation for the Finance Director
drudgery: Rebuilding the same scenario model for every question
Comparing bank and lease offers line by line
today.time_sinks: Building scenarios and lease-versus-buy comparisons from scratch.

lenses.faster: A copilot builds the scenario model from the cash forecast and drafts the offer comparison, so the controller spends time on assumptions and the advice; about a third less time.
lenses.autonomous: Not suitable to run alone; the trigger is a forecast alert, and the copilot prepares the scenarios for the controller.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the site managers: lease-versus-buy advice on every forklift, truck or racking decision, not only big ones; demand would grow because sites now decide these alone.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the model; the controller wants more time negotiating with the bank and lessors.
lenses.options: High value: three to four financing scenarios (facility draw, lease, delay capex, sale-and-leaseback) change which option the Finance Director picks.
lenses.altitude: The controller becomes the treasury adviser who frames the choice and its risks; more expert, with a stronger say in capex timing.
reach: FP&A Analyst: long-term cash and capex modelling
Finance Director: first draft of the bank and lessor negotiation brief

tasks.human_edge: Reading the bank relationship, timing the ask, and judging risk appetite of the owners.
tasks.pattern_why: Each question is different and the recommendation carries judgement and accountability; the person leads.

in_practice.trigger: Cash forecast alert for a gap or surplus, or a capex request above threshold.
steps: Copilot pulls forecast, capex list and current facility terms
Copilot drafts three or four scenarios with cost and cash effect
Controller adjusts assumptions and asks for bank or lessor terms
Controller writes and owns the recommendation
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director and controller decide; any facility or investment follows the mandate register.
in_practice.logs_to: Decision memo with model and prompts stored on SharePoint, not in a personal account.

evidence.claim: The digest places funding and planning advice as copilot at autonomy 2, with cash allocation staying human.
Estimates whose prompt and output sit in a personal account cannot be rebuilt by the auditor.

risks: Wrong assumptions look convincing in a polished model
Model output stored outside company systems
research_questions: How many financing or lease-versus-buy decisions were made last year, and by whom?
Which assumptions changed the outcome most in past decisions?
Would site managers ask for lease advice if it took a day instead of two weeks?

tasks.short: Run the budget cycle and steer planning and purchasing across the three sites and the finance team.

today.trigger: Yearly budget round in autumn, quarterly reforecasts and monthly budget reviews.
steps: Send budget templates in Excel to site and department managers
Chase and consolidate returns
Check against headcount, CAO wage increases and flex worker plans
Run review meetings and agree changes
Load the final budget into AFAS and Power BI
drudgery: Chasing late templates
Consolidating versions of Excel sheets
Recomputing CAO wage effects by hand
today.time_sinks: Version control of budget sheets and repeated chasing of managers.

lenses.faster: A copilot pre-fills site budgets from actuals, CAO increases and the headcount plan and drafts variance notes, so the controller spends time on review meetings; about a quarter less time.
lenses.autonomous: The budget calendar triggers pre-filled templates and reminders; consolidation runs automatically and the controller reviews every change.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to site managers: a monthly rolling forecast per site with flex worker cost by week, instead of a yearly budget; demand would grow because peak season planning depends on it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses merging Excel versions; the controller wants more time challenging plans with site managers.
lenses.options: Useful: two or three budget versions for flex-worker volume and CAO outcome change what the sites commit to.
lenses.altitude: The controller runs the planning process and its assumptions, chairs reviews and sets the challenge; more of a coordinating expert role.
reach: FP&A Analyst: template building and consolidation
HR Business Partner: headcount and flex plan inputs, needing CAO knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating targets with site managers and knowing which numbers are padded.
tasks.pattern_why: The work is coordination and negotiation with people; AI speeds the preparation only.

in_practice.trigger: Budget calendar date or quarterly reforecast.
steps: Pre-fill templates from AFAS actuals, headcount and CAO rates
Send and track returns in Teams
Consolidate and draft variance notes
Controller reviews with managers and approves the final version
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Finance Director approve the budget before it is loaded into AFAS.
data_needed: Actuals by site and cost centre

evidence.claim: Planning and management advice fit a copilot at autonomy 2.

risks: Pre-filled numbers become the budget without real challenge
CAO outcome unknown at budget time
research_questions: How many hours go to consolidation versus review today?
Would site managers use a monthly rolling forecast?
How accurate was the flex worker budget last year per site?

tasks.short: Advise the management team on financial goals, policies and big decisions, short and long term.

today.trigger: Monthly management team meeting, ad hoc questions on pricing, sites or contracts.
steps: Gather figures from Power BI and AFAS
Build analysis in Excel
Write a memo or slides
Present and discuss in the management meeting
drudgery: Pulling the same figures for each question
Formatting slides
today.time_sinks: Building one-off analyses from raw extracts.

lenses.faster: A copilot answers figure questions on the AFAS extract and drafts memos and slides, so preparation drops by about a quarter.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous; a question from management starts it and the controller leads throughout.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the three site managers: a monthly one-page financial briefing per site with plain explanations, which they have never had; demand would grow as they start using it in their own meetings.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting slides; the controller wants more time in the discussion itself.
lenses.options: High value: two or three framed options (for example, raise rates, cut flex hours, renegotiate an agency contract) shape the management decision.
lenses.altitude: The controller spends more time as a business partner in meetings and less building decks; more expert and influential.
reach: FP&A Analyst: ad hoc analysis
Finance Director: first drafts of board memos

tasks.human_edge: Trust with managers, reading the room, and saying an unwelcome thing at the right time.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice depends on context and relationships; the person leads.

in_practice.trigger: Management meeting agenda or ad hoc question.
steps: Copilot pulls figures and drafts the analysis
Copilot proposes two or three options with effects
Controller checks numbers and rewrites the advice
Controller presents
in_practice.human_gate: Controller signs off every memo before it goes to management.

evidence.claim: Advice to management fits copilot, autonomy 2.
Lab results did not measure communication, asking the right questions or tacit context.

risks: Polished drafts with a wrong figure undermine trust
research_questions: What questions did management ask last quarter, and how long did each take?
Would site managers read a monthly briefing?
Which data in the Power BI extract is reliable enough for self-service answers?

tasks.short: Manage absence, disability and liability insurance costs, track rule changes and budget for them.

today.trigger: Policy renewals, UWV notices, yearly budget, rule changes on Ziektewet, WGA or pensions.
steps: Collect premium notices and claims data from insurers and UWV
Check absence data in AFAS against the verzuim policy
Track changes in WIA, Ziektewet and pension rules
Build the budget for premiums and own-risk costs
Discuss renewals with the broker and HR
drudgery: Reading long insurer and UWV letters
Rebuilding the premium budget each year
today.time_sinks: Reading regulation changes and reconciling premium invoices with headcount.

lenses.faster: A model summarises insurer letters and rule changes and drafts the premium budget from AFAS headcount and absence data; the controller checks and decides, saving about 30%.
lenses.autonomous: A new insurer letter or rule change triggers a summary with likely cost effect; the controller reviews before anything goes into the budget.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made more often: quarterly instead of yearly review of the eigenrisicodrager choice for Ziektewet and WGA, given absence trends among shift workers; demand would grow if it took an hour.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reading insurer letters end to end; the controller wants more time on the renewal negotiation.
lenses.options: Useful: comparing being eigenrisicodrager versus public insurance under two absence scenarios changes the choice.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the insurance cost model and renewal strategy with HR; about as expert as today.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: benefit cost budgets
HR Director: insurer renewal brief

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with broker and insurers and weighing risk for the company and works council views.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns letters and rule texts into a checkable summary inside a fixed budget process.

in_practice.trigger: Insurer or UWV letter arrives, or yearly budget date.
steps: Model summarises the document and flags cost effects
Deterministic sheet recomputes premiums from AFAS headcount and absence
Controller reviews and updates the budget
Controller and HR decide on renewals
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every budget change and any renewal decision with HR Director.
in_practice.logs_to: Summary and budget versions on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: The digest places insurance and benefit programmes as llm_step summaries at autonomy 2.

risks: Absence data contains health data under AVG; only aggregated figures may be used
Summary misses a clause with a cost effect
research_questions: Is Noordhaven eigenrisicodrager for Ziektewet or WGA today?
How many hours a year go to insurance work, and how much is reading?
Which absence fields can be used without breaching AVG?

tasks.short: Check payroll deductions and taxes from AFAS payroll and book them correctly in the ledger.

today.trigger: Each monthly or four-weekly payroll run and the loonaangifte.
steps: Receive the payroll journal from the Payroll Specialist
Reconcile wage tax, social premiums, pension and CAO deductions to the general ledger
Check the loonaangifte totals against the journal
Investigate differences and correct postings
drudgery: Ticking payroll totals to ledger accounts
Investigating small rounding and timing differences
today.time_sinks: Finding the cause of differences between payroll, the return and the ledger.

lenses.faster: A reconciliation job ties payroll journal, loonaangifte and ledger each run and lists differences with likely causes; review takes 20 minutes instead of 2 hours.
lenses.autonomous: The payroll run closing in AFAS triggers the tie-out; it passes or flags differences above a threshold for the controller.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made more often: deductions and pension contributions checked on every run, including flex worker cost from agencies, instead of quarterly; demand stays flat, so the value is fewer audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses ticking totals; the controller wants more time on fixing root causes with Payroll.
lenses.options: Little; the result is a tie-out that passes or fails.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the tie-out rules and threshold and reviews exceptions only; job shifts to control design.
reach: Payroll Specialist: first-line reconciliation
Accountant: payroll accruals and holiday pay provisions

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a difference is an error, a timing issue or a CAO rule change, and signing off.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS computes the deductions; the reconciliation is a fixed rule set between three totals.

steps: Extract payroll journal and loonaangifte totals
Tie them to the ledger by component
Flag differences above threshold
Controller reviews and approves or corrects
in_practice.human_gate: Controller signs off flagged differences; the ledger tie-out must be zero before close.
in_practice.logs_to: Reconciliation file on SharePoint for the auditor.

evidence.claim: Nothing should post until bank, AR and AP tie to zero; the tie-out decides.

risks: Rules not updated when the CAO or tax rates change
Payroll data is personal data under AVG
research_questions: How many differences were found per payroll run last year and what caused them?
Does AFAS expose the loonaangifte totals in a readable extract?
Who owns payroll reconciliation today: Payroll Specialist or controller?

tasks.short: Prepare the month-end close, management reports, forecasts, budgets and the yearly accounts for KVK.

today.trigger: Month-end, quarter-end, year-end and the KVK filing deadline.
steps: Direct accountants on accruals, reclasses and reconciliations
Review balances and write flux commentary
Build management reports in Excel and Power BI
Prepare the annual accounts and work with the auditor
Arrange the SBR filing to KVK outside AFAS
drudgery: Rolling forward accruals
Writing variance commentary line by line
Answering repeat auditor questions
today.time_sinks: Accruals, flux commentary and audit queries.

lenses.faster: A model drafts accruals, reclasses and flux commentary, and a tie-out gate blocks posting until bank, AR and AP reconcile; the controller reviews drafts, saving about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: Month-end in AFAS triggers drafts; the controller approves each journal, and nothing posts until the tie-out is zero.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the site managers: a site-level close pack with commentary by working day 5; demand would grow because sites would use it to manage flex cost.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rolling accruals forward; the controller wants more time on judgement items and the forecast.
lenses.options: Moderate: alternative accrual estimates for uncertain items make the judgement explicit for the auditor.
lenses.altitude: The controller moves from preparing the close to designing it: owns the accrual handbook, tie-out queries, materiality thresholds and audit trail; more expert.
reach: Accountant: accrual preparation
FP&A Analyst: flux commentary
Finance Director: first draft of annual report text

tasks.human_edge: Accounting judgement under Dutch GAAP (BW 2 Titel 9), materiality calls and the auditor relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call per item drafts accruals and commentary from messy inputs; a deterministic tie-out gate checks it inside the fixed close process.

steps: Model drafts accruals, reclasses and commentary from AFAS data and the accrual handbook
Deterministic tie-out checks bank, AR, AP and payroll
Controller reviews, adjusts or rejects each draft
Approved journals post in AFAS; reports refresh in Power BI
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every journal; no posting before the tie-out is zero.
in_practice.logs_to: Journal approval log and prompts and outputs on SharePoint for the auditor.

evidence.claim: Trintech's accruals agent generates and rolls forward accruals, flags outliers, then Review & Approve and Retain for Audit.
SAP's accruals agent prepares journals for accountants to accept, adjust or reject; at most five expense categories per handbook.
On 160 US GAAP close tasks the best model meets about 62% of criteria; the bottleneck is accounting judgement.
Accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster across 79 small and mid-sized firms.
Large companies file with KVK via SBR from FY2025; AFAS cannot do this for them.

risks: No product runs on AFAS; integration must be built
Benchmarks are US GAAP; Dutch GAAP untested
Auditor cannot rebuild estimates if prompts are not kept
research_questions: How many days does the close take today and which steps take longest?
Will the auditor accept model-drafted accruals with the logged prompts?
Which accrual categories are stable enough to start with (five or fewer)?
How is the KVK SBR filing done today and by whom?

role.altitude: From preparing the close and approving payments to designing them: the controller owns the accrual handbook, check rules, tie-out queries, materiality and approval thresholds and the audit trail, and spends the freed time as financial adviser to management and the sites.
reach: Bookkeeper: first-line invoice and agency-hours matching
Payroll Specialist: payroll-to-ledger reconciliation
FP&A Analyst: short-term cash forecast and flux commentary
Accountant: accrual preparation
Finance Director: first drafts of board and bank memos
role.ceiling_note: Limited by accounting judgement under Dutch GAAP, signing authority and mandates, the auditor's acceptance of model-drafted estimates, and the lack of ready products on AFAS; about 30-40% of hours on these tasks can go, mostly in checks, reconciliations and drafting.
skills_to_grow: Writing check and tie-out rules on AFAS data
Reviewing and documenting model drafts for audit
role.ambitious_version: Close the month by working day 4 with a site-level pack and a daily cash and covenant view, and offer site managers lease-versus-buy and flex-cost advice they have never had.
